questions.stem: Commerce is best defined as
options: all activities involved in the distribution of goods and services from producers to consumers.
the manufacture of goods in factories.
the extraction of raw materials from the earth.
the buying of goods for personal use only.
questions.explanation: Commerce covers trade and the aids to trade (banking, transport, insurance, communication, warehousing and advertising) that bring goods to consumers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an aid to trade?
questions.explanation: Aids to trade include banking, insurance, transport, communication, warehousing and advertising; the others are production activities.

questions.stem: E-commerce refers to
options: trade between two countries in Europe.
the sale of electrical appliances only.
trade carried on by exchange of goods for goods.
the buying and selling of goods and services over electronic networks such as the internet.
questions.explanation: E-commerce uses websites, mobile apps and electronic payments to carry out commercial transactions.

questions.stem: A major advantage of e-commerce to a small trader in Aba is that
options: she no longer needs to deliver goods to customers.
her goods can never be counterfeited.
she does not need any means of payment.
she can reach customers far beyond her shop without opening new branches.
questions.explanation: Online platforms extend a trader's market to distant customers at relatively low cost.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a risk associated with e-commerce?
questions.explanation: Cyber fraud, identity theft and fake sellers are major disadvantages of e-commerce; the others are advantages.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why commerce is said to "bridge the gap" between producers and consumers?
options: It increases the number of factories in the economy.
It enables consumers to make goods for themselves.
It removes the hindrances of distance, time, risk, finance and information that separate them.
It eliminates the need for money in exchange.
questions.explanation: The branches of commerce overcome hindrances: transport (place), warehousing (time), insurance (risk), banking (finance), advertising and communication (knowledge).

questions.stem: The work a person does regularly to earn a living is called
questions.explanation: An occupation is any regular work done for income.

questions.stem: A teacher, a nurse and a lawyer are engaged in
questions.explanation: Direct services are rendered personally to people; indirect services (such as banking and transport) aid commerce and industry.

questions.stem: A bricklayer building a house is engaged in
questions.explanation: Constructive occupations (building, road and bridge construction) are part of industrial occupations.

questions.stem: Which of the following factors would most influence a young person's choice of occupation?
options: The colour of the uniform worn in the job
Her level of education and training
The number of public holidays in the year
The type of currency used in the country
questions.explanation: Education, aptitude, capital, interest, environment and pay prospects largely determine choice of occupation.

questions.stem: A person who works with a bank, a transport company or an insurance firm is engaged in
questions.explanation: Commercial occupations include trade and the aids to trade.

questions.stem: Production is complete only when
options: goods are stored in a warehouse.
questions.explanation: In commerce, production includes all activities until the goods get to the final consumer.

questions.stem: Mr Bello quarries granite near Abeokuta and sells it to builders. Quarrying granite is an example of
questions.explanation: Primary (extractive) production takes resources directly from nature.

questions.stem: In a garment factory, one worker cuts the cloth, another sews and a third attaches buttons. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Splitting the making of one product into stages, each handled by different workers, is division of labour by process.

questions.stem: One disadvantage of division of labour to workers is
options: monotony and boredom from repeating the same task.
questions.explanation: Repetition of the same simple task can lead to boredom and loss of craftsmanship.

questions.stem: Specialisation makes exchange necessary because
options: a specialist produces more of one item than he needs but lacks other goods he wants.
specialists do not need to consume.
questions.explanation: Since each person produces only a narrow range of goods, he must exchange the surplus for other goods.

questions.stem: Division of labour is limited mainly by
questions.explanation: If the market is small, the increased output from specialisation cannot be sold.

questions.stem: A partnership is a business owned by
options: two or more people who share the profits and losses.
shareholders whose liability is always limited.
questions.explanation: A partnership is an association of two or more persons carrying on business in common with a view to profit.

questions.stem: The document that governs the relationship between partners is the
questions.explanation: The partnership deed sets out capital contributions, profit-sharing ratio, duties and other terms.

questions.stem: A partner who contributes capital but takes no part in the management of the business is
questions.explanation: A sleeping partner provides capital and shares profit but is not active in running the business.

questions.stem: The document that regulates the internal management of a company, such as the rights of shareholders and the powers of directors, is the
questions.explanation: The articles govern the internal affairs; the memorandum (or the company's constitution) shows its relationship with outsiders.

questions.stem: A co-operative society that buys goods in bulk and sells them to its members at reasonable prices is
questions.explanation: Consumer co-operatives buy in bulk and sell to members, sharing any surplus as dividends on purchases.

questions.stem: Members of a thrift and credit society mainly aim to
options: save regularly and obtain loans at low interest.
buy shares on the stock exchange.
questions.explanation: Thrift and credit societies encourage saving and give members cheap loans.

questions.stem: When two or more companies combine to form a new company, it is called
questions.explanation: Amalgamation or merger fuses firms into one, usually to gain economies of scale.

questions.stem: A company that owns more than half of the shares of other companies and controls them is
questions.explanation: The holding company controls its subsidiaries through majority shareholding.

questions.stem: An association of independent firms that agree to restrict output and fix prices, while each keeps its separate identity, is called
questions.explanation: Cartel members remain independent but agree on prices, output or markets.

questions.stem: Under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020, a private company in Nigeria may be formed by
options: a minimum of two persons only.
questions.explanation: CAMA 2020 allows a single person to form a private company; a public company needs at least two members.

questions.stem: The winding up of a company by order of the court, for example because it cannot pay its debts, is called
questions.explanation: Compulsory liquidation is ordered by the court, often on a creditor's petition; voluntary liquidation is decided by the members.

questions.stem: An association formed by firms in the same line of business to protect their common interests is
questions.explanation: Trade associations, such as associations of manufacturers or transporters, protect the interests of firms in a trade.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of a Chamber of Commerce?
options: Organising trade fairs to promote members' products
Fixing the salaries of civil servants
questions.explanation: Chambers of commerce promote trade through trade fairs, information services and representation to government.

questions.stem: The main aim of the Nigeria Employers' Consultative Association (NECA) is to
options: represent employers in negotiations with labour unions and government.
questions.explanation: NECA is the umbrella body of employers in Nigeria and deals with labour and industrial relations matters.

questions.stem: Consumerism refers to
options: the organised effort by consumers to protect their rights against unfair business practices.
the excessive consumption of imported goods.
the policy of producing goods for export only.
questions.explanation: Consumerism is a movement that promotes consumer rights such as safety, information, choice and redress.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of trade associations to consumers is that they may
options: fix prices and restrict competition among their members.
set standards of conduct for members.
questions.explanation: When members agree on prices, consumers lose the benefits of competition.

questions.stem: The total amount of share capital a company is permitted to issue as stated in its constitution is traditionally called
questions.explanation: Authorised or nominal capital is the maximum share capital stated in the company's constitution.

questions.stem: Working capital is calculated as
questions.explanation: Working capital (circulating capital) measures the funds available for day-to-day operations.

questions.stem: A trader has stock ₦450,000, debtors ₦180,000, cash ₦70,000, creditors ₦260,000 and premises ₦2,000,000. Her working capital is
Use the following: opening stock ₦60,000, purchases ₦340,000, closing stock ₦80,000, sales ₦480,000. The gross profit is
From the same data (opening stock ₦60,000, closing stock ₦80,000, cost of sales ₦320,000), the rate of turnover is
A trader's gross profit is ₦150,000 and her net sales are ₦600,000. Her gross profit as a percentage of sales (margin) is
Goods costing ₦800 are sold at a mark-up of 25%. The selling price is
questions.explanation: Mark-up is on cost: 25% of 800 = 200; selling price = ₦1,000.

questions.stem: A company has authorised capital of ₦10m, has issued shares of ₦8m and has called up ₦6m, of which ₦5.5m has been received. Its paid-up capital is
questions.explanation: Paid-up capital is the amount actually received from shareholders on the called-up capital.

questions.stem: Trade credit means that
options: a supplier allows a buyer to take goods now and pay later.
a bank lends money to a customer.
goods are paid for before delivery.
a retailer sells only for cash.
questions.explanation: Trade credit is a short-term source of finance given by suppliers.

questions.stem: A retailer is a trader who
options: sells goods only to other traders.
buys goods in bulk and sells in small quantities to final consumers.
questions.explanation: The retailer is the last link in the chain of distribution.

questions.stem: A small shop in a residential area owned and run by one person is
questions.explanation: A unit (independent) shop is a single outlet, usually a sole proprietorship.

questions.stem: A large shop with many sections under one roof, each selling a different class of goods, is
questions.explanation: A department store is divided into departments (clothing, furniture, cosmetics and so on) under central management.

questions.stem: Chain stores (multiple shops) are characterised by
options: one outlet owned by one person.
many branches with similar appearance and centralised buying.
questions.explanation: Chain stores are many branches owned by one company, with uniform layout and prices and centralised management.

questions.stem: Self-service in a supermarket is an advantage to the retailer mainly because it
options: allows goods to be sold on credit.
reduces the number of sales assistants needed.
questions.explanation: Customers pick goods themselves, so fewer attendants are needed, reducing labour costs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason for the survival of small-scale retailers despite competition from supermarkets?
options: They give credit and personal attention to customers.
They enjoy large economies of scale.
They sell only branded goods at lower prices.
questions.explanation: Personal service, convenient location, credit and flexible hours help small retailers survive.

questions.stem: A wholesaler who takes title to goods, buys them in bulk and resells them at a profit is
questions.explanation: Merchant wholesalers own the goods; agent wholesalers only arrange sales for a commission.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a factor responsible for the elimination of the wholesaler?
options: Small scale retailing by many traders
Production of goods long before they are needed
Manufacturers opening their own retail outlets
questions.explanation: When producers sell directly through their own outlets or to large retailers, the wholesaler is bypassed.

questions.stem: The channel "manufacturer - retailer - consumer" is most likely used when
options: the retailer is a small roadside kiosk.
goods are produced far from consumers in small quantities.
the retailer is a large supermarket chain that buys in bulk.
the manufacturer has no means of transport.
questions.explanation: Large retailers buy direct from manufacturers in quantities big enough to make the wholesaler unnecessary.

questions.stem: A retailer who moves from place to place carrying goods for sale is
questions.explanation: Hawkers carry goods around streets, markets and motor parks.

questions.stem: Trade between Nigeria and Ghana is an example of
questions.explanation: Foreign (international) trade is between countries.

questions.stem: Entrepot trade means
options: importing goods in order to re-export them.
questions.explanation: Entrepot (re-export) trade involves bringing goods in and sending them on to other countries.

questions.stem: The difference between the value of a country's visible exports and visible imports is the
questions.explanation: Balance of trade relates only to visible goods.

questions.stem: An agreement between two countries to trade with each other on agreed terms is
options: a counter trade agreement with many nations.
questions.explanation: Bilateral agreements involve two countries; multilateral agreements involve many.

questions.stem: Counter trade involves
options: payment for imports in foreign currency only.
the exchange of goods for goods between countries.
the importation of goods for re-export.
the ban of a product from a country.
questions.explanation: Counter trade is international barter, for example crude oil exchanged for manufactured goods.

questions.stem: The government agency responsible for collecting import duties at Nigeria's ports and borders is the
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Customs Service collects import and excise duties and checks smuggling.

questions.stem: A clearing and forwarding agent assists an exporter mainly by
options: handling the documentation and shipment of goods through the ports.
insuring the goods against marine risks.
questions.explanation: Clearing and forwarding agents handle customs formalities, documents and arrangements for shipping goods.

questions.stem: A country imposes a tariff on imported shoes mainly to protect local shoe makers. This tariff is meant to
options: reduce the price of local shoes below cost.
make imported shoes dearer than locally made ones.
questions.explanation: Protective tariffs raise the price of imports, helping local infant industries compete.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC)?
options: Encouraging the diversification and growth of non-oil exports
questions.explanation: The NEPC promotes non-oil exports through information, training, incentives and trade missions.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: A document sent by a buyer to a seller requesting the supply of goods is
questions.explanation: The order states the description, quantity and price of goods the buyer wants.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: A document sent by a seller to a buyer showing the goods supplied, their prices and the amount due is
questions.explanation: The invoice is the bill showing goods sold and the amount payable.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: A seller who has overcharged a buyer will correct the error by issuing
questions.explanation: A credit note reduces the amount owed by the buyer (e.g. for overcharges or returns); a debit note increases it.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: A pro forma invoice is sent
options: before the goods are delivered, for example to request payment in advance.
after the goods have been paid for.
by the buyer to the seller.
questions.explanation: A pro forma invoice shows what the bill will be; it is used for advance payment, quotations or import licences.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: "E & OE" printed on an invoice means
questions.explanation: E & OE reserves the seller's right to correct errors and omissions later.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: A quotation of "CIF Lagos" means the price includes
options: cost of goods, insurance and freight to Lagos.
cost of goods only, collected at the factory.
cost of goods and loading onto the ship only.
cost of goods and freight but not insurance.
questions.explanation: CIF covers cost, insurance and freight to the named port of destination.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: A price quoted "ex-works" means
options: the seller delivers to the buyer's premises free of charge.
the price includes freight to the buyer's port.
the goods are on board a ship.
the buyer pays all costs of moving the goods from the seller's factory.
questions.explanation: Ex-works prices cover only the goods at the seller's premises; the buyer bears all transport costs.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: An invoice for goods listed at ₦200,000 offers a trade discount of 10% and a cash discount of 5% for payment within 7 days. If the buyer pays within 7 days, the amount paid is
questions.explanation: Trade discount: 200,000 - 20,000 = 180,000; cash discount: 5% of 180,000 = 9,000; amount paid = ₦171,000.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: A document issued by the consul of the importing country certifying the correctness of the export invoice is a
questions.explanation: A consular invoice, signed by the importing country's consul, helps customs check prices and prevent dumping.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: "COD" on a sales document means
questions.explanation: Under COD the buyer pays when the goods are delivered.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a quality of good money?
questions.explanation: Good money should be durable, portable, divisible, homogeneous, acceptable and relatively scarce.

questions.stem: Cowries, manillas and salt were used as money in West Africa in the past. This shows that money
options: must always be made of paper.
must be issued by a central bank.
is anything generally accepted as a medium of exchange.
questions.explanation: Commodity money shows that acceptability, not material, is what makes something money.

questions.stem: Bank deposits that can be transferred by cheque or electronic transfer are known as
questions.explanation: Bank (deposit) money exists as balances in accounts and moves by cheque or electronic transfer.

questions.stem: Legal tender in Nigeria consists of
options: naira notes and coins issued by the Central Bank of Nigeria.
questions.explanation: Notes and coins issued by the CBN must be accepted in settlement of debts.

questions.stem: When money enables a person to buy a car now and pay for it in instalments over two years, it is performing its function as
questions.explanation: Money allows debts and future payments to be expressed and settled.

questions.stem: The bank that supervises and regulates other banks in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The CBN licenses, regulates and supervises banks and other financial institutions.

questions.stem: An account that is mainly used for day-to-day transactions by cheque or electronic transfer is the
questions.explanation: Current accounts allow frequent withdrawals and cheque use; savings and fixed deposits are for saving.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of a fixed (time) deposit account?
options: Cheque books are issued to the customer.
Withdrawals can be made at any time without notice.
Money is deposited for an agreed period at a higher interest rate.
No interest is paid on the deposit.
questions.explanation: Fixed deposits earn higher interest because funds are tied up for an agreed period.

questions.stem: A bank that grants small loans to low-income earners, artisans and small businesses is
questions.explanation: Microfinance banks provide small loans and savings services to small businesses and low-income earners.

questions.stem: A bureau de change deals mainly in
questions.explanation: Bureaux de change buy and sell foreign currency for travellers and other small users.

questions.stem: An Automated Teller Machine (ATM) enables a bank customer to
options: withdraw cash and check account balance at any time.
buy shares directly from the stock exchange floor.
open a fixed deposit without any bank account.
questions.explanation: ATMs provide round-the-clock cash withdrawal, balance enquiry and other services.

questions.stem: An instruction by a customer to his bank to pay a fixed sum regularly, such as monthly rent, is a
questions.explanation: A standing order is used for regular fixed payments.

questions.stem: A cheque crossed "Account Payee Only" can
options: be cashed over the counter by anyone.
be endorsed to any other person.
only be paid into the bank account of the named payee.
questions.explanation: This special crossing directs the bank to credit only the payee's account, reducing the risk of fraud.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of e-banking to customers?
options: Risk of fraud through phishing and stolen card details
Ability to transfer money at any time
Reduced need to visit the bank hall
questions.explanation: Cyber fraud is a major risk of e-banking; the others are advantages.

questions.stem: Insurance is a device for
options: spreading the losses of a few among many people exposed to the same risk.
questions.explanation: Many people pay premiums into a common pool, from which the few who suffer loss are compensated.

questions.stem: Chidi pays ₦15,000 every month to keep his motor insurance cover in force. This payment is called the
questions.explanation: The premium is the price of insurance cover.

questions.stem: The principle of insurance which requires that a person must suffer financial loss if the insured property is damaged before he can insure it is
questions.explanation: One cannot insure property in which one has no financial interest; otherwise insurance becomes a wager.

questions.stem: Under the principle of indemnity, the insured is compensated
options: with more than the value of the loss so that he makes a profit.
to restore him to the financial position he was in just before the loss.
only if he has never made a claim before.
with the full sum insured whatever the loss.
questions.explanation: Indemnity prevents the insured from profiting from a loss.

questions.stem: After paying compensation for a stolen car, the insurer takes over the right to recover the car if it is found. This is the principle of
questions.explanation: Subrogation gives the insurer the insured's rights against third parties or salvage after paying a claim.

questions.stem: A trader in Onitsha would NOT be able to obtain insurance cover against
options: Loss due to a fall in demand for a trader's goods
Theft of goods from a warehouse
questions.explanation: Speculative business risks such as changes in demand cannot be calculated statistically, so they are uninsurable.

questions.stem: A life assurance policy that pays the sum assured at the end of a fixed period or on earlier death is
questions.explanation: An endowment policy matures after a fixed term or pays on earlier death; whole life pays only on death.

questions.stem: An insurance company that transfers part of a large risk it has accepted to another insurance company is practising
questions.explanation: Reinsurance spreads very large risks among insurers.

questions.stem: Insurance that protects an employer against loss from dishonesty of an employee handling cash is
questions.explanation: Fidelity guarantee covers losses from fraud or embezzlement by employees.

questions.stem: The capital market is a market for
questions.explanation: The capital market deals in long-term securities such as shares and bonds.

questions.stem: The agency that regulates the capital market in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: SEC is the apex regulator of the Nigerian capital market.

questions.stem: When a company offers new shares to its existing shareholders in proportion to their present holdings, it is making
questions.explanation: A rights issue gives existing shareholders the right to buy new shares, usually at a discount.

questions.stem: A company that sells new shares directly to selected institutional investors rather than to the general public is using
questions.explanation: Private placement is a sale of securities to a small group of chosen investors.

questions.stem: In an offer for sale, a company
options: sells shares directly to the public through a prospectus.
sells its shares to an issuing house, which then sells them to the public.
gives shares free to existing shareholders.
invites bids, selling to the highest bidders above a minimum price.
questions.explanation: In an offer for sale the issuing house buys the whole issue and resells it to the public.

questions.stem: The main advantage of a second-tier (growth) market of a stock exchange to small and medium companies is that
options: it allows them to issue currency.
it exempts them from all regulation.
its listing requirements are less strict than those of the main market.
questions.explanation: Lower listing requirements allow growing companies to raise capital publicly.

questions.stem: The organised market where existing shares and bonds are bought and sold in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX), formerly the Nigerian Stock Exchange, is the main securities exchange.

questions.stem: A speculator who buys shares expecting their prices to rise so that he can sell at a profit is called
questions.explanation: Bulls expect prices to rise; bears expect them to fall; stags buy new issues hoping to sell quickly at a premium.

questions.stem: A speculator who applies for new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a profit as soon as trading begins is
questions.explanation: Stags speculate on new issues.

questions.stem: A person who buys and sells securities on the stock exchange on behalf of clients for a commission is
questions.explanation: Stockbrokers act as agents for investors and earn commission.

questions.stem: Government securities, which carry very little risk of default, are known as
questions.explanation: Government bonds are considered very safe, hence "gilt-edged".

questions.stem: The holders of debentures are
options: owners of the company with voting rights.
entitled to the remaining profit after preference dividends.
creditors of the company who receive fixed interest.
questions.explanation: Debenture holders are lenders, entitled to fixed interest whether or not a profit is made.

questions.stem: Which type of shareholder has the right to a fixed rate of dividend before ordinary shareholders are paid?
questions.explanation: Preference shares carry a fixed dividend payable before any ordinary dividend.

questions.stem: A commodity exchange is a market where
options: standardised agricultural and mineral products are bought and sold.
questions.explanation: Commodity exchanges trade graded commodities such as grains, cocoa, cashew and metals.

questions.stem: Before commodities can be traded on a commodity exchange, they must be
questions.explanation: Grading ensures buyers know exactly what quality they are buying without inspecting each lot.

questions.stem: Trading on a commodity exchange in which dealers shout bids and offers on a trading floor is known as
questions.explanation: Open outcry is the traditional floor-trading method; most exchanges now use electronic trading.

questions.stem: A benefit of a commodity exchange to farmers is that it
options: forces them to sell below cost.
removes the need to store produce.
provides a transparent market with fair prices for their produce.
questions.explanation: Commodity exchanges improve price discovery and reduce exploitation by middlemen.

questions.stem: Certified warehouses that issue receipts for stored commodities are important to a commodity exchange because
options: they reduce the quality of commodities.
they allow goods to be sold without grading.
the warehouse receipts can be traded or used as collateral without moving the goods.
they fix the prices of all commodities.
questions.explanation: Warehouse receipts represent title to graded stored goods and can be bought, sold or pledged.

questions.stem: Transport creates
options: form utility by changing the shape of goods.
place utility by moving goods to where they are needed.
questions.explanation: Transport moves goods from places of production to where consumers want them.

questions.stem: The most suitable means for transporting crude oil from oil fields to a refinery is
questions.explanation: Pipelines carry liquids and gases continuously, cheaply and safely over long distances.

questions.stem: Which of the following goods is best sent by air?
questions.explanation: Air transport is fast but expensive, so it suits light, valuable or urgent goods.

questions.stem: A list of all the cargo carried by a ship or aircraft is
questions.explanation: The manifest lists all cargo on board and is used by customs.

questions.stem: A document that accompanies goods sent by road, giving details of the goods and the consignee, is
questions.explanation: A waybill (or consignment note) is the road/rail transport document describing the consignment.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of rail transport over road transport?
options: It is more flexible in routes.
It carries heavy and bulky goods cheaply over long distances.
It is suitable for short distances.
questions.explanation: Railways move large volumes of heavy goods at lower unit cost over long distances.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of water transport is that it
options: is slow and limited to areas with navigable waters and ports.
is the most expensive form of transport for heavy goods.
cannot be used for international trade.
questions.explanation: Ships are cheap for bulky goods but slow and confined to waterways and seaports.

questions.stem: Tourism is
options: travel to places for leisure, business or culture and the services provided for travellers.
the transport of goods by rail.
questions.explanation: Tourism includes travel for recreation, culture or business and the hospitality services involved.

questions.stem: A benefit of tourism to a country such as Nigeria is that it
options: earns foreign exchange and creates jobs in hotels and transport.
raises the prices of local goods.
questions.explanation: Tourism brings income, jobs and foreign exchange; pollution and cultural erosion are disadvantages.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a tourist attraction in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Yankari Game Reserve is in Bauchi State; the others are in other African countries.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of tourism to a host community is that it
options: may erode local culture and encourage social vices.
questions.explanation: Influx of visitors may weaken local customs and promote vices such as drug use.

questions.stem: The sending of messages and information from one person to another is
questions.explanation: Communication is the transfer of information between people.

questions.stem: The postal agency in Nigeria is
options: the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria.
questions.explanation: NIPOST provides postal services; the NCC regulates telecommunications.

questions.stem: Facial expressions, gestures and body movements are examples of
questions.explanation: Non-verbal communication conveys meaning without words.

questions.stem: A courier service is used mainly when
options: documents or parcels must be delivered quickly and securely to the addressee.
bulky goods are to be moved by sea.
crude oil is to be moved to a refinery.
questions.explanation: Courier firms provide fast, tracked door-to-door delivery of documents and parcels.

questions.stem: The physical parts of a computer, such as the keyboard and monitor, are called
questions.explanation: Hardware is the physical equipment; software is the programs that run on it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of using computers in business?
options: Large volumes of data can be processed accurately.
Data can be lost or stolen through viruses and hacking.
questions.explanation: Cyber attacks, viruses and power failures are risks of computerisation.

questions.stem: A warehouse is
options: a shop where goods are sold in small quantities.
a factory where goods are produced.
an office where documents are kept only.
a building where goods are stored until they are needed.
questions.explanation: Warehouses store goods and create time utility.

questions.stem: Warehousing creates
questions.explanation: Storing goods until they are needed makes them available at the right time.

questions.stem: Imported goods on which customs duty has not yet been paid can be kept under customs control in
questions.explanation: In a bonded warehouse, dutiable imports are kept under customs control until duty is paid.

questions.stem: A warehouse owned by a manufacturer to store its finished products is
options: a cold room in a hospital.
questions.explanation: Private warehouses are owned by firms for their own goods; public warehouses store goods for anyone for a fee.

questions.stem: An importer may prefer to keep goods in a bonded warehouse because
options: duty is paid only when goods are withdrawn, which eases the importer's cash flow.
goods there are exempted from all duties.
the warehouse sells the goods on his behalf free of charge.
the goods cannot be inspected by customs.
questions.explanation: Paying duty in instalments as goods are withdrawn means the importer does not tie up capital at once.

questions.stem: Advertising that gives information about the existence, use and price of a product is
questions.explanation: Informative advertising tells consumers about a product's features, use and price.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advertising medium?
questions.explanation: Media include radio, television, newspapers, billboards and the internet.

questions.stem: Advertising aimed at convincing consumers that a product is better than rival brands is
questions.explanation: Competitive advertising seeks to win customers from rival brands.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of advertising to consumers is that it may
options: lead to lower prices through mass production.
persuade them to buy goods they do not need.
questions.explanation: Persuasive advertising can create artificial wants and mislead.

questions.stem: In choosing an advertising medium, a firm should mainly consider
options: the colour of the company's logo.
the target audience and the cost of the medium.
questions.explanation: A firm chooses the medium that reaches its target market most effectively at an affordable cost.

questions.stem: Advertising by a group of producers in the same industry to promote the industry's product generally, rather than a particular brand, is
questions.explanation: Collective advertising, e.g. "Eat more fish", benefits all producers in the industry.

questions.stem: Marketing is concerned mainly with
options: producing as much as possible regardless of demand.
identifying and satisfying customers' needs profitably.
questions.explanation: Marketing identifies, anticipates and satisfies customer needs profitably.

questions.stem: The difference between a market and marketing is that
options: a market is a process, while marketing is a place.
a market is a place or arrangement for buying and selling, while marketing is the process of identifying and satisfying needs.
they mean exactly the same thing.
questions.explanation: Market refers to buyers and sellers in contact; marketing refers to activities that move goods to satisfied customers.

questions.stem: Market research is concerned with
options: the study of all marketing activities of a firm.
gathering information about a particular market, such as customers and competitors.
questions.explanation: Market research studies the market itself; marketing research covers all aspects of a firm's marketing.

questions.stem: Marketing research differs from market research in that marketing research
options: is concerned only with customers' location.
covers all aspects of marketing, including product, pricing, distribution and promotion.
deals only with the stock exchange.
questions.explanation: Marketing research is wider than market research, which concentrates on the market and consumers.

questions.topic: Marketing Concept and the Marketing Mix (4Ps)
questions.stem: The four Ps of the marketing mix are
questions.explanation: The marketing mix combines product, price, place (distribution) and promotion.

questions.topic: Marketing Concept and the Marketing Mix (4Ps)
questions.stem: In the marketing mix, "place" refers to
options: the price charged for the product.
how and where the product is distributed to customers.
questions.explanation: Place covers distribution channels, outlets, transport and stockholding.

questions.topic: Marketing Concept and the Marketing Mix (4Ps)
questions.stem: The marketing concept holds that
options: a firm should produce what it can and then sell it hard.
price is the only factor that matters to customers.
the needs and wants of customers should be the starting point of all business activities.
questions.explanation: Under the marketing concept, firms find out what customers want and produce to satisfy them.

questions.topic: Marketing Concept and the Marketing Mix (4Ps)
questions.stem: A soft drink company introduces a smaller bottle at a lower price for low-income customers. It is mainly adjusting
questions.explanation: A new pack size is a product decision and the lower price is a pricing decision.

questions.topic: Marketing Concept and the Marketing Mix (4Ps)
questions.stem: Packaging and branding are aspects of which element of the marketing mix?
questions.explanation: Branding, packaging, quality and design are product decisions.

questions.stem: Delivery of a refrigerator to the buyer's home and installing it free of charge is an example of
questions.explanation: After-sales services include delivery, installation, repairs and warranties.

questions.stem: A shop attendant explains to a customer how a generator works before the customer decides to buy it. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Pre-sales services help customers make a decision before buying.

questions.stem: Good customer service benefits a business mainly by
options: building customer loyalty and repeat purchases.
questions.explanation: Satisfied customers return and recommend the business to others.

questions.stem: A warranty given by a manufacturer of television sets is important to customers because it
options: guarantees that the price will never change.
allows them to resell the set at a profit.
assures them of free repair or replacement of faulty sets within a stated period.
removes the need for an invoice.
questions.explanation: A warranty protects buyers against manufacturing defects for a stated period.

questions.stem: Free samples, discounts and gifts used to encourage customers to buy are forms of
questions.explanation: Sales promotion uses short-term incentives to boost sales.

questions.stem: A trade fair is important to manufacturers because it
options: is a source of long-term loans.
allows them to display and demonstrate their products to large numbers of buyers.
questions.explanation: Trade fairs bring producers and buyers together for display, contacts and orders.

questions.stem: Personal selling is most suitable for
options: cheap everyday items such as sweets.
expensive technical products such as industrial machinery.
goods sold only by mail order.
questions.explanation: Complex, high-value products need face-to-face explanation and negotiation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a disadvantage of sales promotion?
options: It increases sales in the short term.
Its effect on sales may be short-lived once the incentive is withdrawn.
questions.explanation: Customers may stop buying when the discount or gift ends.

questions.stem: A contract is
options: a promise that cannot be enforced in court.
a legally binding agreement between two or more parties.
questions.explanation: A contract creates obligations enforceable by law.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an essential element of a valid contract?
options: A written letter in all cases
questions.explanation: Valid contracts require offer, acceptance, consideration, intention to create legal relations, capacity and legality.

questions.stem: Consideration in a contract means
options: something of value given by each party in exchange for the other's promise.
the kindness of the parties to each other.
the time taken to reach an agreement.
the place where the contract is signed.
questions.explanation: Consideration is the price for which the promise of the other is bought.

questions.stem: A contract to sell stolen goods is void because
options: the object of the contract is illegal.
questions.explanation: Contracts for illegal purposes cannot be enforced.

questions.stem: A contract is discharged by performance when
options: both parties carry out their obligations as agreed.
the contract becomes impossible to perform.
questions.explanation: Performance by both parties brings the contract to an end.

questions.stem: A singer agrees to perform at a wedding but falls seriously ill and cannot perform. The contract is most likely discharged by
questions.explanation: When unforeseen events make performance impossible without the fault of either party, the contract is frustrated.

questions.stem: A person who acts on behalf of another in dealings with third parties is
questions.explanation: The agent represents the principal and creates contracts binding the principal.

questions.stem: An agent who guarantees the payment of debts by customers he introduces to his principal, in return for extra commission, is
questions.explanation: A del credere agent bears the risk of customers' default for an additional commission.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a duty of an agent to his principal?
options: To delegate all duties to others
To obey the lawful instructions of the principal
questions.explanation: The agent must obey instructions, exercise care, account for money and not make secret profits.

questions.stem: Agency is terminated when
options: the principal dies or the agreed task is completed.
the principal gives the agent new instructions.
the agent sells goods on credit.
questions.explanation: Agency ends by completion, agreement, death, insanity or bankruptcy of either party, and so on.

questions.stem: An agency created when a person acts without authority but the principal later approves the act is
questions.explanation: Ratification is the principal's later adoption of an unauthorised act done on his behalf.

questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act, Hire Purchase Act and Employment Rights
questions.stem: Under the Sale of Goods Act, there is an implied condition that goods sold by description
options: must be paid for in foreign currency.
may be different from the description.
questions.explanation: The buyer is entitled to goods matching the description given.

questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act, Hire Purchase Act and Employment Rights
questions.stem: Under a hire purchase agreement, the ownership of goods passes to the hirer
options: when the last instalment has been paid.
when the first instalment is paid.
questions.explanation: The hirer has possession but not ownership until all instalments are paid.

questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act, Hire Purchase Act and Employment Rights
questions.stem: The amount paid at the beginning of a hire purchase agreement is called
questions.explanation: The hirer pays a deposit and the balance plus interest in instalments.

questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act, Hire Purchase Act and Employment Rights
questions.stem: A television set has a cash price of ₦300,000. On hire purchase, the buyer pays a deposit of ₦60,000 and 12 monthly instalments of ₦23,000. The hire purchase interest is

questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act, Hire Purchase Act and Employment Rights
questions.stem: Which of the following is a right of an employee?
options: To disclose the employer's trade secrets
To receive wages as agreed and work in a safe environment
To use company property for private business
questions.explanation: Employees are entitled to agreed pay, safe conditions, leave and fair treatment.

questions.topic: Government Regulation and Registration of Business
questions.stem: The government agency responsible for registering companies and business names in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The CAC registers companies, business names and incorporated trustees under CAMA 2020.

questions.topic: Government Regulation and Registration of Business
questions.stem: The exclusive right granted to an inventor to make and sell his invention for a period is
questions.explanation: A patent protects inventions; copyright protects literary, artistic and musical works; a trademark protects brand names and logos.

questions.topic: Government Regulation and Registration of Business
questions.stem: A musician's legal protection against others reproducing his songs without permission is
questions.explanation: Copyright protects creative works such as music, books and films.

questions.topic: Government Regulation and Registration of Business
questions.stem: A distinctive name, symbol or logo that identifies a firm's products and is legally protected is
questions.explanation: Registered trademarks prevent others from using the same brand identifiers.

questions.topic: Government Regulation and Registration of Business
questions.stem: A public limited company in Nigeria obtains its legal personality on the issue of
options: a trade licence by the local government.
questions.explanation: On registration, the CAC issues a certificate of incorporation, making the company a legal person.

questions.stem: The government agency in Nigeria that sets and enforces quality standards for products is the
questions.explanation: SON develops and enforces standards for products and processes.

questions.stem: The agency that regulates and controls the manufacture, importation and sale of food, drugs and cosmetics in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) regulates food, drugs and related products.

questions.stem: The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) was established to
options: protect consumers and promote fair competition in Nigerian markets.
questions.explanation: The FCCPC, created by the FCCPA 2018, replaced the Consumer Protection Council.

questions.stem: Consumers need protection mainly because
options: sellers may supply fake, substandard or overpriced goods.
questions.explanation: Consumers are often less informed than sellers and can be exploited.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a way consumers can protect themselves?
options: Buying goods without checking expiry dates
Forming consumer associations to press for their rights
questions.explanation: Consumer associations, careful buying and keeping receipts help consumers seek redress.

questions.stem: The transfer of government-owned enterprises to private ownership is
questions.explanation: Privatisation sells government shares in enterprises to private investors.

questions.stem: The agency responsible for implementing privatisation in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The BPE implements the policies of the National Council on Privatisation.

questions.stem: Deregulation means
options: the government taking over private firms.
the removal of government controls so that market forces determine prices and entry.
questions.explanation: Deregulation reduces government rules and controls on an industry.

questions.stem: Partial commercialisation of a public enterprise means that
options: it is sold completely to private investors.
it receives full government grants for all expenditure.
it is expected to generate enough revenue to cover its operating costs, while government still funds capital projects.
questions.explanation: Partially commercialised enterprises cover running costs; fully commercialised ones fund both running and capital costs.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of privatisation is that it may
options: lead to loss of jobs as new owners cut staff to reduce costs.
questions.explanation: New owners often retrench workers; some services may also become dearer.

questions.stem: The process of planning, organising, directing and controlling the resources of a business to achieve its goals is
questions.explanation: Management coordinates human and material resources to achieve organisational objectives.

questions.stem: The number of subordinates directly supervised by one manager is the
questions.explanation: A narrow span means few subordinates; a wide span means many.

questions.stem: The passing of authority by a superior to a subordinate to carry out specific tasks is
questions.explanation: Delegation transfers authority, though the superior remains ultimately responsible.

questions.stem: The department of a business that is responsible for recruitment, training and welfare of staff is the
questions.explanation: The HR department handles recruitment, training, welfare, discipline and staff records.

questions.stem: A company providing scholarships to students in its host community is showing
questions.explanation: Social responsibility involves contributing to the welfare of society beyond profit-making.

questions.stem: A diagram showing the structure of an organisation, its departments and lines of authority is
questions.explanation: The organisation chart shows positions, departments and reporting relationships.

questions.stem: The headquarters of the ECOWAS Commission is in
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Commission is located in Abuja, Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which of the following countries is a member of the Mano River Union?
questions.explanation: The Mano River Union comprises Liberia, Sierra Leone, Guinea and Côte d'Ivoire.

questions.stem: The Lake Chad Basin Commission has its headquarters in
questions.explanation: The LCBC, created in 1964, is headquartered in N'Djamena, Chad.

questions.stem: One objective of the Lake Chad Basin Commission is to
options: regulate and control the use of the waters and resources of the Lake Chad basin.
issue a common currency for West Africa.
control the price of crude oil.
regulate the stock exchanges of member states.
questions.explanation: The LCBC manages the shared water and natural resources of the basin.

questions.stem: The West African Clearing House was set up mainly to
options: facilitate the settlement of payments for trade among member countries using their own currencies.
regulate fishing on the River Niger.
questions.explanation: The clearing house reduced the use of foreign currencies in intra-regional payments; it later became the West African Monetary Agency.

questions.stem: The European Union is an example of
options: an economic and monetary union of European countries.
questions.explanation: The EU integrates markets and, for many members, uses a single currency (the euro).

questions.stem:
(a) State four features of a partnership. [8 marks]
(b) Explain four ways in which a partnership may be dissolved. [12 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
8 marks: (a) Any four, 2 marks each: owned by two or more persons (usually up to twenty); formed by agreement/partnership deed; capital contributed by partners; profits and losses shared in an agreed ratio; unlimited liability of general partners; no separate legal entity; management shared among active partners; dissolved by death or withdrawal of a partner
12 marks: (b) Any four, explained, 3 marks each: by agreement of the partners; expiry of the agreed period or completion of the venture; death of a partner; bankruptcy/insanity of a partner; by order of court (e.g. misconduct, persistent breach of the agreement); when the business becomes illegal; admission or retirement of a partner (technical dissolution); continuous losses
questions.explanation: (a) A partnership is owned by two or more persons who contribute capital, share profits and losses as agreed, usually bear unlimited liability and are not a separate legal person. (b) A partnership may be dissolved by mutual agreement, expiry of its term or completion of its purpose, death, bankruptcy or insanity of a partner, court order, illegality of the business or continuous losses.

questions.stem:
The following information relates to the business of Mrs Ngozi Okafor for the year ended 31 December 2025:
Stock 1 January 2025: ₦240,000
Stock 31 December 2025: ₦360,000
Purchases: ₦1,620,000
Sales: ₦2,250,000
Returns inwards: ₦50,000
Carriage inwards: ₦40,000
Expenses: ₦210,000
(a) Calculate: (i) net sales; (ii) cost of goods sold; (iii) gross profit; (iv) net profit; (v) average stock; (vi) rate of turnover. [14 marks]
(b) State three ways in which Mrs Okafor can increase her rate of turnover. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Net sales = 2,250,000 - 50,000 = ₦2,200,000
3 marks: (a)(ii) Cost of goods sold = 240,000 + 1,620,000 + 40,000 - 360,000 = ₦1,540,000
2 marks: (a)(iii) Gross profit = 2,200,000 - 1,540,000 = ₦660,000
2 marks: (a)(iv) Net profit = 660,000 - 210,000 = ₦450,000
2 marks: (a)(v) Average stock = (240,000 + 360,000) / 2 = ₦300,000
3 marks: (a)(vi) Rate of turnover = 1,540,000 / 300,000 = 5.13 times
6 marks: (b) Any three, 2 marks each: effective advertising/sales promotion; reducing prices/allowing discounts; improving display and customer service; stocking goods in demand (avoiding slow-moving goods); selling on credit to reliable customers; locating in a busy area; extending opening hours/online sales
questions.explanation: (a) Net sales = ₦2,200,000; cost of goods sold = 240,000 + 1,620,000 + 40,000 - 360,000 = ₦1,540,000; gross profit = ₦660,000; net profit = ₦450,000; average stock = ₦300,000; rate of turnover = 1,540,000 / 300,000 = 5.13 times. (b) She can advertise, cut prices or offer discounts, improve display and service, stock fast-moving goods, give credit to reliable customers and sell online.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a supermarket? [3 marks]
(b) State five features of a supermarket. [10 marks]
(c) Give two reasons why supermarkets may not succeed in rural areas. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) A large self-service retail shop that sells a wide variety of goods, especially groceries and household items, under one roof
10 marks: (b) Any five, 2 marks each: self-service; wide variety of goods; prices clearly marked; goods pre-packaged and branded; cash sales/payment at checkout points; located in towns/shopping centres; large capital required; attractive display; trolleys and baskets provided
7 marks: (c) Any two (4 marks for the first, 3 for the second): low purchasing power of rural dwellers; low population density/small market; preference for bargaining and credit buying; poor infrastructure (power, roads); high illiteracy limiting self-service; consumers buy in very small quantities
questions.explanation: (a) A supermarket is a large self-service store selling a wide range of mainly food and household goods. (b) Features include self-service, wide variety, marked prices, pre-packed and branded goods, cash payment at checkouts, urban location, large capital and attractive displays. (c) Supermarkets struggle in rural areas because of low incomes, small population, preference for haggling and credit, poor infrastructure and very small purchases.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between balance of trade and balance of payments. [6 marks]
(b) Explain four barriers to international trade. [12 marks]
(c) What is entrepot trade? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) Balance of trade is the difference between the value of visible exports and visible imports of a country over a period
3 marks: (a) Balance of payments is a record of all transactions (visible, invisible and capital) between a country and the rest of the world over a period
12 marks: (b) Any four, explained, 3 marks each: differences in currencies/exchange rate problems; language and cultural differences; tariffs and quotas/protectionism; distance and transport costs; complex documentation and customs procedures; risks of goods at sea; differences in weights, measures and standards; political instability/wars; exchange control
2 marks: (c) Entrepot trade is the importation of goods into a country for the purpose of re-exporting them to other countries
questions.explanation: (a) The balance of trade covers only visible goods, whereas the balance of payments covers all external transactions, including services, transfers and capital flows. (b) Barriers include different currencies, language and cultural differences, tariffs and quotas, distance and transport costs, complicated documents, risks, different standards and political instability. (c) Entrepot trade is re-export trade: goods are imported only to be exported again.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem:
(a) Mr Adebayo ordered goods listed at ₦480,000 from a wholesaler. He was allowed a trade discount of 15% and a cash discount of 2.5% for payment within 14 days. He paid within the period. Calculate: (i) the trade discount; (ii) the invoice amount; (iii) the cash discount; (iv) the amount paid. [8 marks]
(b) Explain the following terms used in price quotations: (i) FOB; (ii) CWO; (iii) loco. [6 marks]
(c) State three reasons why a wholesaler grants trade discount. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) Trade discount = 15% x 480,000 = ₦72,000
2 marks: (a)(ii) Invoice amount = 480,000 - 72,000 = ₦408,000
2 marks: (a)(iii) Cash discount = 2.5% x 408,000 = ₦10,200
2 marks: (a)(iv) Amount paid = 408,000 - 10,200 = ₦397,800
2 marks: (b)(i) FOB (free on board): the price covers the goods and all costs until they are loaded on board the ship; the buyer pays freight and insurance thereafter
2 marks: (b)(ii) CWO (cash with order): the buyer must pay when placing the order
2 marks: (b)(iii) Loco: the price covers the goods only at the seller's premises; the buyer bears all costs of collection and transport
6 marks: (c) Any three, 2 marks each: to encourage bulk buying; to allow the retailer a margin to cover expenses and profit; to attract and retain customers; to allow the retailer to sell at the recommended retail price; to clear old stock
questions.explanation: (a) Trade discount = ₦72,000; invoice amount = ₦408,000; cash discount = 2.5% of 408,000 = ₦10,200; amount paid = ₦397,800. (b) FOB covers costs up to loading on the ship; CWO requires payment with the order; loco means the price at the seller's premises with the buyer bearing all further costs. (c) Trade discount encourages bulk purchases, gives retailers a margin, attracts customers, supports recommended retail prices and clears stock.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a current account and a savings account. [8 marks]
(b) Explain four forms of electronic banking available to customers in Nigeria. [12 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
8 marks: (a) Any four contrasts, 2 marks each: current account allows cheques while savings account usually does not; current account holders may obtain overdrafts, savings account holders usually cannot; current account usually earns little or no interest while savings earns interest; current account is mainly for business/frequent transactions while savings is for saving; current account attracts bank charges; minimum opening requirements differ (e.g. references for current account)
12 marks: (b) Any four, explained, 3 marks each: Automated Teller Machines (cash withdrawal, balance enquiry, transfers); internet banking (transfers, bill payments online); mobile banking apps and USSD codes; Point of Sale (POS) terminals for card payments; debit/credit cards for online and in-store payments; electronic funds transfer (instant transfers between banks); SMS/e-mail alerts
questions.explanation: (a) A current account is for frequent transactions, uses cheques, can carry an overdraft, attracts charges and pays little interest; a savings account is for saving, earns interest and generally has no cheque facility. (b) E-banking includes ATMs, internet banking, mobile apps and USSD, POS terminals, payment cards, instant electronic transfers and transaction alerts.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following principles of insurance: (i) utmost good faith; (ii) insurable interest; (iii) indemnity; (iv) contribution. [12 marks]
(b) State four benefits of insurance to a business. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) Utmost good faith: both parties, especially the proposer, must disclose all material facts truthfully; non-disclosure makes the contract voidable
3 marks: (a)(ii) Insurable interest: the insured must have a financial interest in the subject matter, so that he suffers loss if it is damaged
3 marks: (a)(iii) Indemnity: the insured is restored to the position he was in before the loss, not allowed to profit
3 marks: (a)(iv) Contribution: where the same risk is insured with more than one insurer, the insurers share the loss in proportion, and the insured cannot recover more than the loss
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: compensation for losses enables business to continue; encourages investment/risk taking; insurance policies serve as security for loans; provides funds for investment; reduces anxiety; promotes foreign trade (marine insurance); provides employment; loss prevention advice
questions.explanation: (a) Utmost good faith requires full disclosure; insurable interest requires financial interest in the subject matter; indemnity restores the insured to the pre-loss position; contribution shares the loss among insurers covering the same risk. (b) Insurance compensates losses, encourages enterprise, serves as collateral, mobilises funds, reduces anxiety and supports foreign trade.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a stock exchange? [3 marks]
(b) State five functions of the stock exchange. [10 marks]
(c) Explain the following types of speculators: (i) bull; (ii) bear. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) An organised market where existing securities (shares, stocks and bonds) of listed companies and government are bought and sold, such as the Nigerian Exchange (NGX)
10 marks: (b) Any five, 2 marks each: provides a market for buying and selling securities; helps companies and government raise long-term capital; ensures liquidity of investments; indicates the value of securities/economic barometer; protects investors through rules and regulation; encourages savings and investment; facilitates mergers and acquisitions; publishes information about companies
4 marks: (c)(i) Bull: a speculator who buys securities expecting prices to rise in order to sell later at a profit
3 marks: (c)(ii) Bear: a speculator who sells securities expecting prices to fall, hoping to buy them back later at a lower price
questions.explanation: (a) A stock exchange is an organised, regulated market for existing securities, such as the NGX in Lagos. (b) It provides a market for securities, helps raise long-term capital, makes investments liquid, values securities, protects investors, encourages saving and investment and facilitates mergers. (c) A bull buys expecting a rise in price; a bear sells expecting a fall.

questions.stem:
(a) A manufacturer in Kano wants to send goods to customers in Lagos. Identify five factors she should consider before deciding which means of transport to use. [10 marks]
(b) Explain the advantages of pipeline transport. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: (a) Any five, 2 marks each: cost of transport; nature of goods (perishable, fragile, bulky); urgency/speed; distance; safety and security; availability of the means; flexibility/door-to-door service; reliability
10 marks: (b) Any five, 2 marks each: cheap to operate after installation; continuous flow of goods; not affected by weather; reduces road congestion and damage; less labour required; safe and reliable; suitable for liquids and gases over long distances
questions.explanation: (a) The choice depends on cost, nature of the goods, urgency, distance, safety, availability, flexibility and reliability. (b) Pipelines carry liquids and gases continuously and cheaply after installation, are not affected by weather, ease road congestion, need little labour and are safe.

questions.stem:
(a) What is communication? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four services of the Nigerian Postal Service (NIPOST). [12 marks]
(c) State two disadvantages of the internet in business communication. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) The process of transmitting information, ideas or messages from one person or place to another
12 marks: (b) Any four, explained, 3 marks each: ordinary mail/letters; registered post; parcel post; express mail service (EMS)/speed post; post office boxes and private mail bags; money orders/postal orders; agency services (e.g. collection of fees, stamp duty, licences); philatelic services
5 marks: (c) Any two (3 marks for the first, 2 for the second): risk of hacking and cyber fraud; viruses; dependence on electricity and network availability; cost of devices and data; spam and misinformation; low internet penetration in rural areas
questions.explanation: (a) Communication is the transfer of messages and information. (b) NIPOST provides ordinary and registered mail, parcels, express mail, post office boxes and private mail bags, postal and money orders and agency services. (c) Internet communication faces cyber fraud, viruses, power and network problems, costs and poor rural access.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain four functions of a warehouse. [12 marks]
(b) Describe the following types of warehouse: (i) bonded warehouse; (ii) public warehouse. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
12 marks: (a) Any four, explained, 3 marks each: storage of goods until needed (time utility); stabilisation of prices; protection of goods from damage and theft; facilitates continuous production; breaking bulk, grading and packaging; enables seasonal goods to be available all year; bonded storage facilitates payment of duty in instalments; serves as a distribution point
4 marks: (b)(i) Bonded warehouse: owned or approved by customs, used to store imported dutiable goods until duty is paid; goods may be repackaged or re-exported without duty
4 marks: (b)(ii) Public warehouse: owned by government or a private firm and rented to anyone who wants to store goods for a fee
questions.explanation: (a) Warehouses store goods, stabilise prices, protect goods, support continuous production, break bulk and grade goods, make seasonal goods available year-round and allow phased payment of duty. (b) A bonded warehouse holds dutiable imports under customs control until duty is paid; a public warehouse rents space to any member of the public.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain four advantages of advertising to the manufacturer. [12 marks]
(b) State four advertising media available to a business in Nigeria. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
12 marks: (a) Any four, explained, 3 marks each: increases sales and turnover; introduces new products; builds brand loyalty/image; meets competition; leads to mass production and lower costs; creates awareness of the firm; reduces the need for sales personnel
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: newspapers and magazines; radio; television; billboards/posters; internet and social media; cinema; transit advertising (vehicles); handbills/direct mail; SMS advertising
questions.explanation: (a) Advertising boosts sales, launches new products, builds brand loyalty, helps meet competition, enables mass production and creates awareness. (b) Media include newspapers, magazines, radio, television, billboards, the internet and social media, cinema, vehicles and handbills.

questions.topic: Marketing Concept and the Marketing Mix (4Ps)
questions.stem:
(a) What is the marketing mix? [4 marks]
(b) Explain each of the four elements of the marketing mix. [16 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) The combination of controllable marketing variables (product, price, place and promotion) that a firm uses to satisfy its target market
4 marks: (b) Product: the goods or services offered, including quality, design, branding, packaging and after-sales services
4 marks: (b) Price: the amount charged, including pricing strategy, discounts and credit terms
4 marks: (b) Place: how the product reaches consumers, including channels of distribution, outlets, transport and stock levels
4 marks: (b) Promotion: communicating with customers through advertising, sales promotion, personal selling and publicity
questions.explanation: (a) The marketing mix is the blend of product, price, place and promotion used to meet customer needs. (b) Product concerns what is offered; price, what is charged; place, how it is distributed; promotion, how customers are informed and persuaded.

questions.stem:
(a) State five elements of a valid contract. [10 marks]
(b) Explain five ways in which a contract may be discharged. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: (a) Any five, 2 marks each: offer; acceptance; consideration; intention to create legal relations; capacity of the parties; legality of the object; genuine consent; possibility of performance; certainty of terms
10 marks: (b) Any five, 2 marks each: performance; agreement; breach; frustration/impossibility of performance; operation of law (e.g. death, bankruptcy); lapse of time
questions.explanation: (a) A valid contract needs offer, acceptance, consideration, intention to create legal relations, capacity, legality, genuine consent and certainty. (b) Contracts are discharged by performance, agreement, breach, frustration, operation of law and lapse of time.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain four ways in which agency may be created. [12 marks]
(b) State four duties of a principal to his agent. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
12 marks: (a) Any four, 3 marks each: by express appointment (oral or written, e.g. power of attorney); by implication from conduct or relationship; by ratification; by necessity (emergency); by estoppel; by operation of law
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: pay the agreed commission; reimburse expenses properly incurred; indemnify the agent against losses incurred in lawful performance; provide the agent with necessary information and facilities; not to prevent the agent from earning commission
questions.explanation: (a) Agency may arise by express appointment, by implication, by ratification, by necessity, by estoppel or by operation of law. (b) The principal must pay commission, reimburse expenses, indemnify the agent and give necessary information and facilities.

questions.stem:
(a) What is consumer protection? [3 marks]
(b) State three reasons why consumers need protection. [6 marks]
(c) Explain the roles of the following agencies in protecting consumers in Nigeria: (i) NAFDAC; (ii) Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON); (iii) Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC). [11 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) The measures taken by government, consumers and organisations to safeguard consumers against exploitation and unfair practices by producers and sellers
6 marks: (b) Any three, 2 marks each: to prevent sale of fake/adulterated goods; to prevent exploitation through excessive prices; to prevent false/misleading advertisement; to protect health and safety; to prevent short weights and measures; to provide redress for injured consumers
4 marks: (c)(i) NAFDAC regulates the manufacture, importation, distribution and sale of food, drugs, cosmetics, chemicals and packaged water; registers such products and removes fake ones
4 marks: (c)(ii) SON sets and enforces standards for products, inspects products and certifies quality (e.g. product certification and conformity assessment of imports)
3 marks: (c)(iii) FCCPC protects consumer rights, investigates complaints, ensures fair competition and sanctions unfair practices
questions.explanation: (a) Consumer protection is the safeguarding of consumers against exploitation and unsafe goods. (b) Consumers need protection against fake goods, exploitative prices, misleading adverts, unsafe products and short measures. (c) NAFDAC regulates food and drugs; SON sets and enforces quality standards; FCCPC handles consumer complaints and promotes fair competition.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of: (i) privatisation; (ii) commercialisation; (iii) deregulation. [9 marks]
(b) State four reasons why government privatises public enterprises. [8 marks]
(c) Give one disadvantage of deregulation. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) Privatisation: transfer of ownership of government enterprises (shares/assets) to private individuals or firms
3 marks: (a)(ii) Commercialisation: reorganising public enterprises to operate profitably without subsidies while remaining government-owned
3 marks: (a)(iii) Deregulation: removal of government controls and restrictions so that market forces determine prices and entry into an industry
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: to improve efficiency; to reduce the financial burden of subsidies; to raise revenue for government; to attract foreign and private investment; to reduce political interference and corruption; to broaden share ownership; to improve service quality
3 marks: (c) Any one: higher prices of goods and services; exploitation by private monopolies; loss of government control over strategic sectors; job losses
questions.explanation: (a) Privatisation transfers ownership to private investors; commercialisation keeps government ownership but requires profitable operation; deregulation removes controls so markets decide prices and entry. (b) Governments privatise to improve efficiency, cut subsidies, raise revenue, attract investment, reduce interference and improve services. (c) Deregulation can raise prices and expose consumers to private monopolies.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following terms: (i) delegation of authority; (ii) span of control; (iii) responsibility. [9 marks]
(b) State four functions of management. [8 marks]
(c) Give one reason why inter-departmental communication is important. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) Delegation: the passing of authority by a superior to a subordinate to perform specific tasks while the superior remains accountable
3 marks: (a)(ii) Span of control: the number of subordinates directly supervised by a manager
3 marks: (a)(iii) Responsibility: the obligation of a subordinate to perform assigned duties and account for them
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: planning; organising; staffing; directing/leading; coordinating; controlling; motivating
3 marks: (c) Any one: ensures coordination of activities; avoids duplication and conflict; speeds decision-making; promotes efficiency and team spirit
questions.explanation: (a) Delegation transfers authority downwards; span of control is the number reporting directly to a manager; responsibility is the duty to perform assigned tasks. (b) Management functions are planning, organising, staffing, directing, coordinating, controlling and motivating. (c) Communication between departments ensures coordination and avoids duplication.

questions.stem:
(a) State four objectives of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS). [8 marks]
(b) Explain four achievements of ECOWAS. [12 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
8 marks: (a) Any four, 2 marks each: promote trade among members; free movement of persons, goods and services; common external tariff; harmonise agricultural, industrial and monetary policies; develop regional infrastructure; promote peace and security; raise living standards
12 marks: (b) Any four, explained, 3 marks each: protocol on free movement allowing visa-free entry for citizens; ECOWAS Trade Liberalisation Scheme; adoption of a common external tariff; peace-keeping (ECOMOG) and conflict resolution; ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID) financing projects; ECOWAS Court of Justice and Parliament; regional infrastructure projects such as the West African Gas Pipeline and road corridors; ECOWAS passport/biometric identity card
questions.explanation: (a) ECOWAS aims to promote trade, free movement, a common external tariff, harmonised policies, regional infrastructure, peace and higher living standards. (b) Achievements include visa-free movement, trade liberalisation, the common external tariff, ECOMOG peace-keeping, EBID project finance, regional institutions and infrastructure such as the West African Gas Pipeline.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a commodity exchange? [4 marks]
(b) State four requirements for trading on a commodity exchange. [8 marks]
(c) Explain four benefits of a commodity exchange to the economy. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) An organised market where standardised and graded commodities (agricultural produce, minerals) are bought and sold, either for immediate or future delivery
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: grading; standardisation; warehousing in certified warehouses; clearing and settlement system; registration of traders/brokers; adequate quantity of commodity
8 marks: (c) Any four, 2 marks each: fair price discovery; reduces exploitation of farmers by middlemen; stabilises prices; provides market information; encourages production; provides access to finance through warehouse receipts; earns foreign exchange; reduces post-harvest losses
questions.explanation: (a) A commodity exchange is an organised market for standardised commodities. (b) Trading requires grading, standardisation, certified warehousing, a clearing system and registered participants. (c) Exchanges improve price discovery, protect farmers, stabilise prices, provide information, encourage production and ease access to finance.
